identity.title: Standard Gaussian Process is All You Need for High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization

problem.claim: Whether standard Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization can perform well in high-dimensional optimization.

gap.claim: The belief that standard BO underperforms in high dimensions lacked robust empirical evidence and theoretical justification.

contributions.claim: A systematic evaluation reports that Matérn kernels enable standard BO to achieve top-tier results across twelve benchmarks, often surpassing methods designed for high-dimensional optimization.

A theoretical analysis attributes the SE kernel’s failure primarily to commonly used length-scale initialization that can cause gradient vanishing; probabilistic bounds characterize the issue and indicate greater robustness of Matérn kernels at higher dimensions.

A robust initialization strategy for the SE kernel is proposed, reportedly bringing its performance close to state-of-the-art without additional priors or regularization, with a further probabilistic bound addressing gradient vanishing.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a systematic empirical and theoretical re-evaluation of standard BO in high-dimensional settings, together with a simple robust SE-kernel initialization strategy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report results from a comprehensive evaluation across twelve benchmarks: SE kernels often perform poorly, whereas Matérn kernels consistently achieve top-tier results and frequently surpass specialized high-dimensional methods.

The authors report a probabilistic bound characterizing the SE length-scale initialization problem and showing that Matérn kernels are less susceptible and can handle much higher dimensions more robustly.
The authors report that their initialization strategy dramatically improves SE-kernel performance, bringing it close to state-of-the-art, and provide a bound showing mitigation of gradient vanishing.

narrative_sequence.summary: A prevailing belief says standard BO with standard GPs underperforms in high-dimensional optimization, but the belief lacks robust evidence and theory.
The paper introduces a systematic investigation of standard BO’s high-dimensional behavior.
Across twelve benchmarks, kernel choice differentiates outcomes: SE often performs poorly, while Matérn frequently outperforms specialized methods.
The analysis links SE failure to length-scale initialization and gradient vanishing, then proposes robust initialization and supporting probabilistic bounds.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a comparative evaluation with a proposed mechanism: kernel-dependent performance patterns are followed by an explanation involving length-scale initialization and gradient vanishing.

lessons.interpretation: This pairing can make an empirical claim more informative by connecting observed differences to a testable technical cause.
lessons.application: When reporting a method comparison, separately state the performance pattern and formulate a measurable mechanism that could explain it, then connect the intervention to that mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the study has no plausible mechanism or lacks measurements that distinguish competing explanations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the twelve benchmarks, dimensions, baselines, metrics, or statistical details behind the reported comparisons.
The exact initialization strategy, probabilistic bounds, assumptions, and meaning of “close to state-of-the-art” are unspecified.
The abstract does not report numerical effect sizes, uncertainty, or whether all claims hold uniformly across tested settings.
